labels.note: Nature 1998 paper; title, authors, journal, year, DOI and PMID match R1 original. DOI as written has a trailing period; PMID alone identifies the paper.
Standaert 2011 Spine; R1 is a Cochrane spinal manipulation review, different paper. DOI (Spine prefix) and PMID presented together in one cite; no record contradicts.

Chou 2007 Ann Intern Med. DOI 10.1001/archinte.147.3.492 looks like an Arch Intern Med style DOI, inconsistent with the cited journal/issue; item cannot show whether DOI and PMID name one work or which identifier fits the cited paper. R1/R2 are Cochrane reviews on other topics.
Lee & Done 2004 CD003281.pub2 (P6 stimulation); R1 is a different Cochrane review (CD004125).

Unit cites Ezzo 2006 review (pub2), matching R2 original by title, year, DOI, PMID. R1's original is the 2000 first version; its notice DOI equals the unit's DOI (pub2 is the document that withdrew pub1), so by identifier the unit cites R1's notice document, though it is cited as a source work.
Trinh 2007 Spine (DOI 10.1097/brs, PMID 17224820), a different publication than the Cochrane versions in R1-R4 (none has this DOI/PMID); records reached only by title tokens.
Cochrane CD003788.pub2 acupuncture for rheumatoid arthritis 2005; R1 is a Best Pract Res Clin Rheumatol paper with another DOI and title.
Lau et al. 2010 J Virol; title, journal, year, DOI, PMID all match R1 original.

Title, journal, year, volume/pages and PMID match R1 original. Unit DOI differs from R1 original DOI (10.2174/1389203711213080012); item does not show whether both DOIs name one work. PMID alone identifies the paper.
Palfreyman 2006 Cochrane (pub2): matches R2 by title, year, DOI, PMID. R1 is the 1998 first version, a different document with different DOI.
Ma et al. 2017 Nature paper; title, DOI, PMID match R1 original. No notice identifiers in the record; unit is the paper.
